source.title: Conversion therapy: an evidence assessment and qualitative study — Appendix 1: Glossary
source.scope_note: Definitions describe this report's usage. Source attestation does not validate a universal archive definition or a SOGICE relationship.
source.definition_representation: Researcher-authored concise summaries of the source definitions, not verbatim transcriptions.

terms.source_definition: A person who does not experience sexual attraction.
Attraction to more than one sex or gender.
Gender identity corresponds with sex recorded at birth.
Interventions intended to change sexual orientation or gender identity.
Identity used after conversion efforts when a person no longer identifies as lesbian, gay, or bisexual.
Religious setting or organisation providing conversion-oriented activity.
Religious self-help movement organised around unwanted same-sex attraction.
Emotional, romantic, or sexual orientation toward the same sex or gender.
Diagnosis involving distress related to incongruence between sex and gender identity.
How a person outwardly expresses gender.
A person's internal sense of gender.
Interventions intended to change a transgender identity toward cisgender identity.
Incongruence between sex and gender identity, whether or not it causes distress.
The Equality Act protected characteristic associated with proposing, starting, or completing transition.
Attraction to another or opposite sex or gender.
Attraction to the same sex or gender; also described as gay.
Umbrella term for variations in sex characteristics outside typical male or female expectations.
A woman whose orientation is toward women or the same sex or gender.
Report umbrella for minority sexual orientations and gender identities.
Report category covering transgender and non-binary identities and histories.
Report category for sexual orientations other than heterosexual.
Gender identities that are not exclusively man or woman.
Attraction that is not limited by sex or gender.
Minority sexual-orientation or gender-identity term with both reclaimed and historically derogatory uses.
A specific conversion-therapy approach associated with Moberly and Nicolosi.
The report's category based on birth registration and physical sex characteristics.
Natural change in attraction or identity, distinguished from deliberate change efforts.
A label used to describe orientation, which may differ from attraction or behaviour.
Emotional, romantic, or sexual attraction.
Interventions intended to change a minority sexual orientation toward heterosexuality.
Attraction to another or opposite sex or gender; heterosexual.
Gender identity differs from sex recorded at birth.
Historical diagnostic term superseded by later diagnostic language.
Change-seeker term used in place of a lesbian, gay, or bisexual identity.
Congenital chromosomal, gonadal, anatomical, or hormonal sex-characteristic variation.
